_comment: Skill Repo Spec v1 s9 -- every path in this repo belongs to exactly one class.
FIXTURE = lifelike test data, must be produced by tools/make_fixtures.py.
DATA    = anything a real run produced. Never git-tracked; resolved out-of-repo by tools/datadir.py.
data_sealed = a path that HELD real data, was purged, and must stay dead.
Enforced by tools/data_boundary.py in .githooks and CI.
_audited: 2026-07-31 RE-AUDIT (CORRECTS the 2026-07-20 sweep, which recorded that llmcall 'is not appended, cached or journalled anywhere, in this repo or outside it'. That was wrong). llmcall DOES produce real-run output: core.py keeps a provider-mix ledger, one JSONL line per call recording which provider actually served, so that silent provider degradation is visible. It carries no prompt and no reply text (both are recorded as CHAR COUNTS) and it is on by default. Its home is ~/.llmcall/ledger.jsonl, outside every repo; $LLMCALL_LEDGER overrides the path and 0/off disables it. The other writes really are transient: tempfile.mkstemp files for codex stdin/stdout, unlinked after use. Nothing repo-relative is written by default, so there is still no path to declare here, but the reason is 'the ledger lives elsewhere', not 'there is no ledger'.
_armed: 2026-07-31 ARMED. The empty declaration above stopped being the control on this date. An independent verifier cloned this repo, committed metrics/live-runs.jsonl and runs/transcript.json into it, and tools/data_boundary.py exited 0: checks 1..3 only ever inspect what the manifest DECLARES, so a manifest that declares nothing was enforcing nothing, and the careful paragraph above was doing the work a check is supposed to do. Check 4 now runs off the TRACKED FILE LIST instead and fails any file wearing the shape of real-run output (a jsonl under metrics/, a runs/ tree, a dated file under an output dir, a live-ledger filename, a database) whether or not this manifest declares a thing. So the empty `data` list is a claim re-tested on every commit and in CI, not a note taken on faith. That distinction is load-bearing here: the provider-mix ledger defaults to ~/.llmcall/ledger.jsonl but $LLMCALL_LEDGER sets the path and a relative value lands wherever the caller's cwd is, so 'the default resolver points elsewhere' was never the same statement as 'nothing can land here'.
